messages.text:
We propose giving one external color specialist access to first-batch master images for calibration. We would identify the specialist to the archive for written approval and require the specialist to sign the same confidentiality terms before access begins. The specialist would use a read-only workspace with downloads disabled. We would revoke access when calibration ends or five calendar days after access begins, whichever comes first. If full-page access is unacceptable, would the archive approve crops showing the color target and representative paper and ink tones, with no legible text?

Within the studio, only assigned scanning and quality-control staff would have access. For each batch, we propose keeping working files for ten calendar days after delivery so the archive can flag defects and we can correct them. We would delete active copies at the end of day ten. If a correction reported by then is still open, we would retain only the affected files, agree on a new deletion date with the archive in writing, and delete them sooner if the correction is delivered earlier. Encrypted backup copies would be accessible only to backup administrators for disaster recovery and would expire within 45 days of active deletion. We would reapply deletions after any restore and confirm final expiry in writing.

For publicity, we request permission to publish one anonymized process photograph on the studio’s website showing the scanning setup, with no readable correspondence, donor identifiers, or identifying metadata. We would submit the exact image and caption for separate written approval before publication. Would those limits work for the archive?

We can agree to the following terms for the signed schedule.

- **Calibration and access.** We’ll supply a calibration sheet. Two donor collections are restricted to archive personnel. The archive will identify them before transfer and keep their originals and unmasked images out of the studio workflow. For other collections, only assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff may view full pages. If the sheet proves insufficient, one named external specialist may view crops from those other collections after we approve the specialist and the exact crops in writing. Crops may show the target, blank paper and isolated ink tones. Mask all handwriting and identifying details and strip metadata before review. We accept your confidentiality, read-only and download controls. Revoke access when calibration ends or after five calendar days, whichever comes first.
- **Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days from batch delivery for active quality-control files. For a defect reported within that window, retain only the affected files under a deletion date agreed in writing before day ten ends. Delete them on delivery of the correction or on the agreed date, whichever comes first. Please confirm active deletion in writing by batch, identifying any files still held and their deletion date. We propose a maximum of **30 calendar days after active deletion** for encrypted backups, with your administrator-only recovery controls and reapplication of deletions after a restore. Please confirm final expiry by batch in writing, with the date. If 45 days is a technical minimum, please identify the constraint so we can decide that exception before signing.
- **Incidents.** Before transfer, list a monitored incident email and phone number for each party. The studio should notify the archive promptly, within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized viewing or disclosure, including by the specialist. Send the initial notice with the facts available, then update us on affected batches and containment.
- **Publicity.** We can consider one equipment-only photograph for the studio website. Stage it with an empty scanner bed and keep collection material, screen content and identifiers out of the frame. Strip identifying metadata and submit the exact image and caption for separate written approval before publication. Signing the schedule grants no publication permission.

Can the studio meet the 30-day backup limit and the incident terms? If the calibration sheet and approved crops are insufficient, full-page specialist access would remain an unresolved request for the other collections. The two restricted collections are excluded from any such exception.

We can meet the incident terms. Our backup system runs on a fixed 45-day rotation, so we cannot guarantee expiry within 30 calendar days of active deletion. We request a 45-calendar-day maximum for encrypted backups only. Access will be limited to backup administrators for disaster recovery, and we will reapply deletions after any restore. For each batch, we will confirm active deletion in writing, identify any files retained for a timely reported defect and their agreed deletion date, and confirm final backup expiry in writing with the date.

Before transfer, we will provide our monitored incident email and phone number and record the archive’s contacts alongside ours. We will notify the archive promptly and within 24 hours of discovering any suspected loss, unauthorized viewing or disclosure, including an incident involving the specialist. We will send the facts available at discovery and follow up with affected batches and containment measures.

We accept the ten-day correction window and the proposed deadlines for deleting affected files. We also accept the exclusions for the two restricted collections. For other collections, we will start with the calibration sheet and use the specialist only under the approval, masking, metadata and access controls you specified. If approved crops prove insufficient, we will pause the affected calibration and consult the archive. Any request for full-page specialist access would require a separate written agreement.

We accept the equipment-only photograph terms, including an empty scanner bed and separate written approval of the exact image and caption before publication on the studio website.

Can the archive approve the 45-day backup exception for the signed schedule?

Yes. The archive approves a maximum of **45 calendar days after active deletion** for encrypted backup copies. Record this as the sole retention exception. Access is limited to backup administrators for disaster recovery. The studio will reapply deletions after any restore and confirm both active deletion and final backup expiry in writing for each batch, with the dates and any agreed defect holds. The ten-day active-file limit and agreed correction deadlines still apply.

With that exception recorded, the schedule is agreed. We’ll provide our monitored incident email and phone number before transfer. Full-page specialist access remains outside the signed scope. If approved crops prove insufficient, pause the affected calibration. Any request for broader access to the other collections requires a separate written agreement. The two restricted collections remain archive-only.

Masking the first test crop removed an ink-tone feature the specialist needs to verify. We have paused the affected calibration. Would the archive select one nonrestricted sample that preserves the feature and authorize a single supervised, on-premises review in a separate written agreement? The agreement would identify the specialist, sample and feature in advance. The specialist would view only the area needed on a read-only studio workstation, with the rest of the page masked. An archive representative could inspect the prepared view before the specialist sees it and supervise throughout. We would disable downloads and printing, prohibit photography and end access at the close of the session. If the archive prefers, it could supply a calibration sheet that reproduces the missing feature for us to test first.

For rescans, we propose an acceptance test **before delivery of the correction**, so the operator can verify the result while the working copy is still available. For each reported defect, we would agree with the archive in writing on a pass criterion. For this color defect, that would mean identifying the reference ink tone, the comparison method and the acceptable tolerance. Assigned studio quality-control staff would check the corrected master against that criterion and verify that the delivery file opens and preserves the result.

On a pass, we would deliver the correction with the test result and delete the working copy on delivery. On a failure, we would report the result and retry within the existing deadline. The ten-day limit, any timely agreed defect hold and the backup expiry terms would still apply. Would the archive accept a documented studio test on that basis?

We accept the documented studio test for rescans. For the paused calibration, we propose using a nonrestricted comparison sheet selected by our conservator. Only a masked image of that sheet may leave the archive. Donor letters, including images and crops, may not be supplied or shown to the specialist.

We’ll prepare a masked view that preserves the ink-tone feature for the specialist to assess under the agreed access controls. If that view is insufficient, we can offer one supervised morning next week **at the archive** to compare it with the original. Before that session, we’ll agree in writing on the specialist, sheet, feature and date. The conservator will inspect the prepared view, expose only the necessary area of the original and supervise throughout. The original stays at the archive. No photography, printing or copying is permitted. Access ends when the session closes, and the studio must delete any separate specialist review copy and confirm deletion in writing.

The specialist may advise on the comparison sheet. The archive’s conservator will approve the reference tone, comparison method and tolerance in writing. Assigned studio quality-control staff will test the scan against those criteria and verify that the delivery file opens and preserves the result. **Unaffected scanning may proceed.** For the affected work, test scans may proceed once the criteria are agreed. Production scanning may resume once the conservator reviews the documented pass and releases the calibration in writing.

For rescans, deliver a passing correction with its test result and delete the working copy on delivery. Report a failure and retry within the existing deadline. A failed test does not extend retention. Delete active files by the end of day ten after batch delivery, except for files covered by a timely written defect hold. Delete held files on delivery of the correction or on the agreed deletion date, whichever comes first, even if the defect remains open. Confirm active deletion by batch and confirm final encrypted backup expiry within 45 calendar days after active deletion.

Can the studio proceed with the masked comparison sheet first and, if original review is needed, confirm the named specialist’s morning availability next week?

Yes. We can proceed with the conservator’s masked comparison sheet under the agreed access controls. The specialist’s review will be limited to that sheet. We will delete any separate specialist review copy when the review ends and confirm deletion in writing.

If the masked view is insufficient, we accept one supervised morning at the archive under the proposed restrictions. The specialist’s availability is unconfirmed. Please send the conservator’s available morning dates and times for next week. We will check them with the specialist and, if a visit is needed, confirm the specialist’s name, sheet, feature and appointment with you in writing before the visit.

Unaffected scanning can proceed. For the affected work, we will begin test scans once the conservator approves the reference tone, comparison method and tolerance in writing. Production will resume only after the conservator reviews the documented pass and releases the calibration in writing.

We accept the rescan and deletion terms. Assigned quality-control staff will test the corrected master and verify that the delivery file opens and preserves the result. We will deliver a passing correction with its test result and delete the working copy on delivery. If a test fails, we will report it and retry within the existing deadline. We will confirm active deletion and final backup expiry by batch under the agreed schedule.

The schedule is agreed. Please proceed with the masked comparison sheet and unaffected scanning. The specialist’s review is limited to the comparison sheet. For affected work, test scans may begin once the conservator approves the color criteria in writing. Production may resume after the conservator reviews the studio’s documented pass and gives written clearance. The agreed deletion deadlines apply throughout.

One morning next week is available for a supervised review at the archive. We still need to confirm the exact date and time with the conservator. We’ll send the slot once confirmed. If the masked review proves insufficient, we’ll confirm the specialist, sheet, feature and appointment with you in writing before the visit.
